The page renders its static markup, `blazor` initialises, and\\nthen the runtime dies at startup with:\\n\\n```\\nError: AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage (Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:\\nhttp://127.0.0.1:5300/_framework/resource-collection.ty4X_.js)\\nTypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../_framework/resource-collection.ty4X_.js\\n    at un (.../_framework/dotnet.runtime..js)\\n    at rn.resolve_or_reject (.../_framework/dotnet.runtime..js)\\n    ...\\n    at .../_framework/dotnet.native..wasm:wasm-function[298]\\n```\\n\\nNothing is rendered by any `InteractiveWebAssembly` component; the page sits on its static content.\\n\\n**It is load-dependent, not random.** With one browser at a time it does not occur at all. With eight\\nconcurrent browsers it affects roughly half of page loads.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe runtime starts on every load. Concurrency between independent browser instances should not affect\\nwhether an app boots.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n**Repro: https://github.com/Memphizzz/BlazorBootBugRepro**\\n\\n```bash\\ngit clone https://github.com/Memphizzz/BlazorBootBugRepro\\ncd BlazorBootBugRepro \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; ./repro.sh\\n```\\n\\nStock template, stock Chrome, no test framework and no third-party packages. The **only** addition to\\nthe template is a component rendered with `prerender: false`, so the marker it renders can come from\\nnowhere but a started runtime. The repo is the output of:\\n\\n```bash\\ndotnet new blazor -o BootRepro --interactivity WebAssembly --empty\\n```\\n\\n`BootRepro.Client/Booted.razor`:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\u003cp\\u003eWASM-BOOTED\\u003c/p\\u003e\\n```\\n\\nappended to `BootRepro/Components/Pages/Home.razor`:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\n```\\n\\nThen run N headless Chrome instances at the same URL, each with a fresh profile, and count the DOMs\\nthat do not contain the marker:\\n\\n```bash\\nfor i in $(seq 1 8); do\\n  google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-first-run \\\\\\n    --user-data-dir=\\u0026#34;$(mktemp -d)\\u0026#34; --virtual-time-budget=20000 \\\\\\n    --dump-dom \\u0026#34;http://127.0.0.1:5299/\\u0026#34; \\u0026gt; out-$i.html 2\\u0026gt;/dev/null \\u0026amp;\\ndone\\nwait\\ngrep -L wasm-booted out-*.html      # every file listed never started the runtime\\n```\\n\\n**Measured on the stock template above** (.NET 10.0.111, Chrome 143, Ubuntu 26.04):\\n\\n| concurrency | page loads | never started the runtime |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| **1 at a time** | 8 | **0** |\\n| **8 at a time** | 48 | **25** |\\n\\nThe serial arm is the control: same app, same browser, same budget, same marker — only concurrency\\ndiffers, so this is not the dump being taken too early.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n```\\nTypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:\\n  /_framework/resource-collection..js\\n```\\nsurfaced as `AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage` from `dotnet.runtime..js`. It reaches\\n`console.error` only — it raises no `error` or `unhandledrejection` event, so a page-level error hook\\nsees nothing.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.111\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n**ASP.NET Core**: 10.0.11 · **Chrome**: 143.0.7499.109 · **OS**: Ubuntu 26.04 (x64), WSL2 ·\\nno IDE (CLI).\\n\\n**Additional evidence from a private harness, offered because it narrows the mechanism.** The same\\nfailure occurs there, and a Chrome net-log (`--log-net-log`) of a failing browser shows:\\n\\n- **No `URLRequest` is issued for that module on the failing load** — not an error, not a hang: no\\n  request. The bytes never being asked for is the finding, and it is why raising client timeouts\\n  changes nothing.\\n- Across **1,522** `_framework` requests in that browser: **zero** ended with a `net_error` and\\n  **zero** never completed.\\n- When the module *is* requested it is served correctly — `200`, `Content-Type: application/javascript`,\\n  gzip, full length — so this is not the server, the MIME type, or the fingerprint.\\n- A per-load table across three non-victim browsers: **22 of 22** first-of-test loads fetched the\\n  module, no exceptions. A failing load is the one that did not ask for it.\\n\\n**Note on the resource**: `resource-collection.{fingerprint}.js` does not exist on disk; it is\\ngenerated and served by middleware (see #62249). We have not established whether that is relevant.\\n\\n**Why this repo**: the failing import is of a Blazor asset produced by the ASP.NET Core static-asset /\\nimport-map machinery, and the repro is a Blazor template — so `aspnetcore`. The stack, however, is\\ninside `dotnet.runtime.js` and `dotnet.native.wasm`, so if the defect is in the runtime\\u0026#39;s startup\\nimport path this belongs in `dotnet/runtime` and we would expect a transfer rather than a close.\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68697\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Memphizzz\",\"id\":4660924,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Memphizzz\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/4660924?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Needs: Attention :wave:\"],\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":1},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-21T16:31:27Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-25T13:23:46Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

I did not want to deal with hosting them on separate paths (through things like `` as it involved an existing application which would have been difficult to migrate, so they are exposed on separate domains. \\n\\nTo separate their assets I have been using \\u0026#34;StaticWebAssetBasePath\\u0026#34; in the csproj\\u0026#39;s to g et two folders in the wwwroot (say app-1 and app-2). So for the sake of discussion, i have app.com which gets (largely) served from wwwroot/app-1 and my.app.com which gets (largely) served from wwwroot/app-2. They are both able to use the same api which is accessible by route /api/xxx.\\n\\nSome issues I had with this are that the server had to be modified slightly to point the applications to the correct paths for certain requests (mostly different PathBase)\\n- the `_content` directory is  published in the wwwroot instead of wwwroot/app-1, requests to assets here seem to work with the PathBase changes on the server.\\n- resourcecollection.{fingerprint}.js and blazor.web.js do not exist on disk but generated by some middleware, it wont be served correctly unless the request pipeline has the correct PathBase set (app-1/app-2).\\n- _framework/dotnet.js will not be found with these PathBase changes on the server. I have to manually prepend the PathBase _again_ to find the file like `/app-1/app-1/_framework/dotnet.js`. \\n\\nSo at this point I hack in a little middleware that essentially checks for any path `some.file` if `{pathbase}/some.file` exists on disk. Note that this does mean we are already looking for `app-1/_framework/dotnet.js` so we add the \\u0026#34;missing\\u0026#34; segment.\\n\\nNow here we are, up and running. A bit wacky that is has to be like this but sure. However, I noticed that fingerprinting is now suffering from the same weird double PathBase requirement issue:\\n- Like with _framework/dotnet.js, I am already effectively serving `/app-1/app-1/main.js`. Even though the browser thinks its serving `/main.js`. To reiterate, I have to .UsePathBase in program.cs AND the middleware that adds the pathbase again, to the actual request path.\\n- The fingerprinded asset paths (resolved in App.razor through the ComponentBase.Assets property) do not work either unless the path base is included in the path `/app-1/main.js`. \\n\\nIn the last point, I would be adding the pathbase THREE times. Amazingly, this would in turn break the resolution of _framework.dotnet.js and my middleware hack (which I am not keen on keeping) cannot work around this by checking for a file on disk, because only the StaticAssetsEndpointDataSource which knows which file the path may map to.\\n\\nSo I have gotten a bit stuck here. \\n\\n\\n\\n\\n  \\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\n1. Static asset requests involving assets in a StaticAssetsBasePath directory need not add multiple PathBase\\u0026#39;s in the request uri to be resolved, wether they are fingerprinted or not. \\n2. Fingerprinting url resolution considers the StaticAssetsBasePath\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nSample blazor web repo + add an extra client.\\n\\nServe each client from a separate \\u0026#39;sub application\\u0026#39; using `MapWhen(ctx =\\u0026gt; domain == x, app =\\u0026gt; configureApp(app)`. and configure each app with a separate PathBase and UseEndpoints with MapStaticAssets and MapRazorComponents/MapRazorPages.\\n\\nThen set the StaticAssetsBasePath in each blazor client\\u0026#39;s csproj file, matching the respective pathbases ofcourse.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n9.0.203\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/62249\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"ArcadeMode\",\"id\":5969155,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/ArcadeMode\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/5969155?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"investigate\",\"area-blazor\"],\"assignees\":[\"javiercn\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-06-04T19:19:54Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-01-25T10:07:44Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

etc.)\\n\\n### Describe the solution you\\u0026#39;d like\\n\\nThe following code should work without any issues since I\\u0026#39;m isolating the two clients using a request filter, as proposed in the ASP.NET 7 tutorial.\\n\\n```\\n            app.UseHttpsRedirection();\\n            app.UseRouting();\\n            app.UseStaticFiles();\\n            app.UseAntiforgery();\\n\\n            app.MapWhen(ctx =\\u0026gt; ctx.Request.Host.Port == 7282, client1 =\\u0026gt;\\n            {\\n                client1.Use((ctx, nxt) =\\u0026gt;\\n                {\\n                    if (!ctx.Request.Path.Value!.Contains(\\u0026#34;blazor.web.js\\u0026#34;))\\n                    {\\n                        ctx.Request.Path = \\u0026#34;/Client1\\u0026#34; + ctx.Request.Path;\\n                    }\\n                    return nxt();\\n                });\\n\\n                client1.UseStaticFiles();\\n                client1.UseStaticFiles(\\u0026#34;/Client1\\u0026#34;);\\n                //client1.UseRouting(); //\\u0026lt;--- needed???\\n                client1.UseEndpoints(endpoints =\\u0026gt;\\n                {\\n                    endpoints.MapRazorComponents()\\n                        .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode()\\n                        .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode()\\n                        .AddAdditionalAssemblies(typeof(Client.Pages.Counter).Assembly);\\n                });\\n            });\\n\\n\\n            app.MapWhen(ctx =\\u0026gt; ctx.Request.Host.Port == 7283, client2 =\\u0026gt;\\n            {\\n                client2.Use((ctx, nxt) =\\u0026gt;\\n                {\\n                    if (!ctx.Request.Path.Value!.Contains(\\u0026#34;blazor.web.js\\u0026#34;))\\n                    {\\n                        ctx.Request.Path = \\u0026#34;/Client2\\u0026#34; + ctx.Request.Path;\\n                    }                    \\n                    return nxt();\\n                });\\n\\n                client2.UseStaticFiles();\\n                client2.UseStaticFiles(\\u0026#34;/Client2\\u0026#34;);\\n                //client2.UseRouting(); //\\u0026lt;--- needed???\\n                client2.UseEndpoints(endpoints =\\u0026gt;\\n                {                    \\n                    endpoints.MapRazorComponents()\\n                        .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode()\\n                        .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode()\\n                        .AddAdditionalAssemblies(typeof(MultiClientTest.SecondClient.Pages.Counter).Assembly);\\n                });\\n            });\\n            \\n            app.Run();\\n```\\n\\nAlternatively you could offer an optional builtin feature for isolating multiple client apps, like so:\\n\\n```\\napp.MapRazorComponents(ctx =\\u0026gt; ctx.Request.Host.Port == 7282)\\napp.MapRazorComponents(ctx =\\u0026gt; ctx.Request.Host.Port == 7283)\\n```\\n\\nI\\u0026#39;m aware that this could still lead to ambiguous route mappings if the request filters aren\\u0026#39;t mutually exclusive; In `App.razor`, when the global render mode of `` and `` is null because `HttpContext.AcceptsInteractiveRouting()` is `false`, I included `WasmStarter` with Blazor WASM render mode. This allows Blazor WASM to download and start in the background while users interact with the static SSR-enabled page content! ❤️\\n\\nThis approach works, but with these two issues:\\n\\n1- When navigating from a static SSR-enabled page to a Blazor WASM page, Blazor sends an unnecessary XHR request to fetch that page(!). A fix would be nice]\\nProblem: [Error 400][A valid antiforgery token was not provided with the request. Add an antiforgery token, or disable antiforgery validation for this endpoint] for a **static** SSR page, related to the constant antiforgery token update, if the redirect was from __another__ domain.\\n\\nI created a new default project BWA i-auto (i(nteractive)-server \\u0026amp; i-wasm) + \\u0026#34;include sample pages\\u0026#34; in the latest VS 17.11.4 . I am attaching the project [BlazorApp2.7z](https://aka.ms/dc/file?name=B[REDACTED]_BlazorApp2.7z\\u0026amp;tid=[REDACTED]), it is a default + one simple test page (/test) with an edit form only.\\n\\nIf you open the /test page in a new tab and click submit - then the page works;\\nThen if you open another /weather (sr-s-SSR=streaming rendering static SSR) page in a new tab from another domain - the previous page immediately gives 400 when submitting the form. (demonstrated in the video [bandicam 2024-10-06 13-32-03-490.mp4](https://aka.ms/dc/file?name=B[REDACTED]_bandicam_2024-10-06_13-32-03-490.mp4\\u0026amp;tid=[REDACTED]))\\nThe problem is that the antiforgery token is updated if the redirect was to a new tab from another domain (demonstrated in the video [bandicam 2024-10-06 13-48-18-096.mp4](https://aka.ms/dc/file?name=B[REDACTED]_bandicam_2024-10-06_13-48-18-096.mp4\\u0026amp;tid=[REDACTED])). The server IIS logs contain a new AF-token only for the last POST request to which the server responded with a 400 error.\\nIf you repeat this situation with opening the /weather page in a new tab with _manual_ input of the url - then there is **no** such problem.\\n\\nIs this a bug or some kind of Blazor technology issue for static pages? Can MS solve it?\\n\\nThe sample is temporarily deployed blazorapp220241005182634.azurewebsites.net\\n\\nPossible **workaround 1** for a s-SSR page: So far I see this workround:\\nUse a js function that will check that the AF-token has not changed after loading the page and pressing the submit button. If it has changed, refresh the page (the AF-token will be updated automatically) or first ask the user to confirm that the page should be refreshed.\\nBut af-token cannot be read from cookies by design as \\u0026#34;Httponly cookies\\u0026#39; purpose is being inaccessible by script.\\u0026#34;\\n\\nThe question: **How to find out with JavaScript that the AF-token has changed (a boolean sign is enough)?**\\n\\nPossible **workaround 2** for a s-SSR page:\\nWhen pages (like /weather) load, they detect that the token has changed and write the current timestamp to the browser\\u0026#39;s local storage. The test page, when a button is pressed, will detect that the state has changed (compare the timestamps via JS).\\n\\nThe question: **How to find out with C# (OnInitializedAsync) that the AF-token has changed (a boolean sign is enough)?**\\n\\n---\\n### Original Comments\\n\\n#### Feedback Bot on 10/7/2024, 08:21 PM: \\n\\n\\u003cp\\u003eWe have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. Action { get; set; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe login should complete without any errors and the user should be authorized.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nI analysed the **AuthenticationService.js** file and the **RemoteAuthenticationService** class and debugged them step by step.\\n\\nWhat I\\u0026#39;ve noticed is that **CompleteSignInAsync** \\n```csharp\\nvar result = await JsRuntime.InvokeAsync\\u0026gt;(\\u0026#34;AuthenticationService.completeSignIn\\u0026#34;, context.Url);\\n```\\nreturns null - although in the browser storage i can see MSAL entries.\\n\\nI modified the AuthenticationService.js and mocked the completeSignIn method like this:\\n```js\\nasync completeSignIn() {\\n            console.warn(\\u0026#34;SIGN IN MOCKED!\\u0026#34;);\\n\\n            return {\\n                status: \\u0026#34;success\\u0026#34;,\\n                state: {\\n                    returnUrl: \\u0026#34;http://localhost:5175/\\u0026#34;\\n                }\\n            };\\n        }\\n```\\nI attached a logger to the **IJSRuntime InvokeAsync** methods  and noticed that when **CompleteSignIn** is called by the **RemoteAuthenticationService** it quickly returns null. The .NET/JS interop can continue using shared memory if we find it\\u0026#39;s necessary to have good perf on those older browsers (and thread safety is not difficult because it\\u0026#39;s all synchronous).\\n * **In a web worker (background thread) on more up-to-date browsers**. The .NET/JS interop will need to work by serializing any data that is being transferred rather than passing pointers [1].\\n\\nThis will be advantageous because then, even if your .NET code does something that locks up the CPU (such as a GC cycle), the UI will remain perfectly smooth (e.g., during animations or scrolling, or while the user is typing quickly into a textbox).\\n\\nThe existing UI update mechanism is designed around transferring batches of minimal diffs from .NET to JS, so it shouldn\\u0026#39;t be hugely difficult to have it express those diffs as serialized data rather than pointers into the WASM memory space. We\\u0026#39;ll have to be careful around things like event handling to ensure that the asynchrony can\\u0026#39;t result in inconsistency of behaviour versus the synchronous single-threaded model. For example, we will need to force all event delivery to be async as far as the JS side is concerned, even in the non-worker-thread case.\\n\\n*[1] Strictly speaking, we could also do it with shared memory on even newer browsers that support SharedArrayBuffer. But if we can get satisfactory perf without this, it would be better to serialize because it would mean fewer combinations of browser scenarios, and saves us having to deal with potentially complex thread-safety concerns on the .NET side.*\",\"state\":\"open\",\"state_reason\":\"reopened\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/5475\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"severity-minor\",\"affected-very-few\",\"not-on-roadmap\"],\"assignees\":[\"pavelsavara\"],\"milestone\":\".NET 12 Planning\",\"comments\":14,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":22,\"+1\":21,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":1,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2018-02-19T17:05:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T12:05:29Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":67768,\"title\":\"Run Blazor WebAssembly in a Web Worker\",\"state\":\"CLOSED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67768\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For example:\\n\\n * Render batches are communicated to JS via zero-copy shared memory rather than by serialization\\n * Events triggered from JS are always processed synchronously by .NET, so there\\u0026#39;s no need to queue them\\n\\nAt first glance, it appears to work with `true`, but that\\u0026#39;s a mirage: it does *not* guarantee correctness in that mode, because the core single-threadedness assumption is violated. For example, JS might raise event 2 before event 1 finished processing, and by the time event 1 is done, there might not even be an event 2 handler any more and then you have an error.\\n\\n### Why we\\u0026#39;re only just encountering this now\\n\\n1. We didn\\u0026#39;t have multithreading before\\n2. Even to the extent that we did have an early preview of multithreading, it worked by running .NET on the browser UI thread, so we could define that as the sync context and then all the same assumptions would remain valid within that sync context. But now .NET WebAssembly has just moved to the new \\u0026#34;deputy thread\\u0026#34; multithreading model (i.e., all .NET code is on a background worker), these assumptions are no longer valid (e.g., because the UI thread\\u0026#39;s JS can no longer communicate with .NET in a synchronous, blocking manner).\\n\\n### Ensuring correctness\\n\\nWe\\u0026#39;ve already solved all these problems in our other hosting environments, Server and WebView, because they\\u0026#39;ve always been innately asynchronous from the beginning. We would need to generalize/port all these mechanisms so they are shared with or copied by the WebAssembly renderer, JS interop, eventing system, etc.:\\n\\n- [ ] Change rendering to serialize renderbatches to JS instead of doing shared-memory reads\\n- [ ] Change the rendering flow so that the renderer\\u0026#39;s `UpdateDisplayAsync` returns a `Task` that doesn\\u0026#39;t complete until the JS side sends back an explicit acknowledgement of that renderbatch\\n- [ ] Review JS interop to make sure any low-level assumptions we\\u0026#39;ve made about synchrony during the internals of message passing are replaced by async assumptions\\n- [ ] Do the above without changing things for the **single-threaded** WebAssembly flavour, since (1) it would be breaking if for example synchronous UI updates became async, and (2) those perf optimizations are there for a reason, and we don\\u0026#39;t want to make rendering many times more expensive in cases where you\\u0026#39;d be serializing huge strings, for example. It\\u0026#39;s OK to have significant behavioral and performance changes when people opt into multithreading, but not when they don\\u0026#39;t.\\n\\n### Approach\\n\\nAs a broad strategy, I think we can:\\n\\n * Factor out some new `WebRenderer` subclass called something like `AsyncWebRenderer` that holds the common logic around serializing renderbatches and accepting the async renderbatch acknowledgements from JS. This can then be used by all of Server, WebView, and multithreaded-WebAssembly.\\n * Use our WebView implementation as the reference for how a complete, async-safe rendering and eventing model should work, because this was more recently implemented than Server and is generally simpler and cleaner. There\\u0026#39;s not a huge amount of code in it, really. If some extra work is needed to queue event notifications, for example, we should see that clearly from the WebView code.\\n\\nI suspect it\\u0026#39;s not necessary to have two different builds of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly`. The total amount of code that should differ between the threaded and not-threaded won\\u0026#39;t be very much. I expect we can just have two different `Renderer` subclasses and some if/else branches in the JS code.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54365\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"triaged\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-threading\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":26,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":47,\"+1\":30,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":17,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-03-05T10:02:51Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-04-21T00:06:24Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":true,\"has_children\":false,\"parent\":{\"number\":17730,\"title\":\"Real multithreading in Blazor WebAssembly\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17730\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

When navigating to `/error`, the Error page is rendered statically on the server, then when the client app starts, overwrites the Error page with the NotFound page content on the client. \\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe default project should demonstrate how to mix server-rendered and client-rendered content properly in the same app. Currently, the default project itself demonstrates mixing the render modes incorrectly.\\n\\nWhile putting `@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` can be considered a workaround, it is undesirable: the layout of the application itself might still be using WebAssembly for even simple interactivity, like collapsing menus. `ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting` bypasses starting the WebAssembly runtime altogether.\\n\\nPossible solutions:\\n- Mark server-rendered content to persist on the client after client interactive routing kicks in. Possibly a marker attribute on the element, a directive, or an `@attribute` similar to `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute`.\\n- Allow `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute` to actually initialize the WebAssembly app, but leave the components marked with this attribute as-is in the DOM. Consider renaming the attribute if so. This might be easy to do using similar mechanics as seen in `PersistentState`\\n- Allow customizing the `Router`. For example, allow a behavior that lets the router \\u0026#34;keep\\u0026#34; the content as-is when a navigation event occurs, by overriding/passing `OnNavigatingAsync` or similar, or by inheriting from the built-in `Router`.\\n- Allow supplying a custom `Router` altogether. This would also allow multiple additional scenarios if community-built routers were to show up: handling localization in the URL, multiple hierarchic routers, etc.\\n- Allow rendering content on the server and let the client WebAssembly app \\u0026#34;consume\\u0026#34; the rendered static HTML as interactive. This might be a stretch, but for some simple cases, it can work.\\n- Modify/implement a new `RenderMode` that allows server-client handoff.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n`dotnet new blazor --name BlazorSSRCSR --all-interactive --interactivity WebAssembly`\\n`cd BlazorSSRCSR`\\n`dotnet run`\\n\\nNavigate to the created app\\u0026#39;s `/error` endpoint. The endpoint will show the server side error, then after a short time, the client side router overwrites the content with the client side `NotFound` page content.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.100-rc.1.25451.107\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nThis is NOT the same as similar (possibly slightly related) issues:\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38128\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/42561\\n\\nNote that there\\u0026#39;s also the implication that if this is done, \\u0026#34;mixing\\u0026#34; render modes across a hierarchy might become possible. That would also require the user be able to set `RenderMode` to `Static` explicitly, which is currently not possible because it\\u0026#39;s not even defined in `RenderMode`: it\\u0026#39;s condered `Static` rendering when the `RenderMode` evaluates to `null`.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/63842\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"yugabe\",\"id\":14803737,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/yugabe\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/14803737?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-09-26T13:34:52Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-02-13T11:20:42Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

With `blazor.web.js` the options are grouped, `{ ssr: {...}, circuit: {...}, webAssembly: {...} }`, but with `blazor.server.js` or `blazor.webassembly.js` the runtime-specific options were top-level properties instead. Guidance and samples written for one kind of app did not apply to another, and a block of options could not be moved between them. ([#51611](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/51611))\\n\\n.NET 11 accepts the grouped format in all three scripts. This validates that the grouped format now works everywhere, and that apps written the older flat way keep working untouched.\\n\\n## Minimum build\\n\\n.NET 11 Preview 7 or later.\\n\\n## Configurations to cover\\n\\n* Blazor Web App\\n  * [ ] Static SSR\\n  * [ ] Interactive Server\\n  * [x] Interactive WebAssembly\\n  * [ ] Interactive Auto\\n* [x] Standalone WebAssembly\\n* [ ] Hybrid (MAUI)\\n\\n## Also exercise\\n\\n* [x] Published output\\n* [ ] An existing .NET 10 app upgraded to .NET 11\\n* [ ] Trimming or ahead-of-time compilation\\n* [ ] More than one server instance, or a proxy in front\\n* [ ] Hot Reload\\n* [ ] An IDE as well as the command line\\n* [ ] Container\\n\\n## Setup\\n\\nAlongside the app types in the list above, building a Blazor Server app that loads the server script directly is worthwhile, since that is the other place these options are written.\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nA standalone WebAssembly app that configures its own startup: set the logging level, supply the environment, and hook into the startup process so you can tell from the console that your configuration ran. Write these options in the newer nested style. Then make a second copy that writes the same options in the older flat style, and a third that mixes the two, setting some options one way and some the other. Do the same for a Blazor Server app that loads the server script directly, so you can compare the two app types.\\n\\n## Things to try\\n\\n* Running each copy and comparing what the console shows.\\n* Setting the same option in both styles at once with different values, to see which wins.\\n* Writing an option name that does not exist, or misspelling one.\\n* Copying a block of options from the Blazor Web App documentation into the standalone app unchanged.\\n* Publishing the apps and running the published output.\\n* Looking for documentation that tells you which style to use, and noting how easy it was to find.\\n\\n## Expected behavior\\n\\nOne block of startup options can be written once and used in any app type, and existing apps are unaffected.\\n\\n### Must hold\\n\\n* The same block of options written in the newer nested style is accepted by each app type covered, without being rewritten between them.\\n* An app written in the older flat style keeps working, with no new warning and no change in behavior.\\n* Where both styles set the same option, the outcome is the same on every run rather than depending on the order the options appear in.\\n* An option name that does not exist fails in a way a developer can notice, rather than being silently ignored.\\n\\n### Expected differences between configurations\\n\\n* No differences are expected.\\n\\n## Documentation to use\\n\\n* [Blazor startup options release notes](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-11#blazor-web-script-startup-options-format-now-supported-for-blazor-server-and-blazor-webassembly-scripts)\\n* [ASP.NET Core Blazor startup](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/blazor/fundamentals/startup?view=aspnetcore-11.0)\\n* [ASP.NET Core Blazor logging](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/blazor/fundamentals/logging?view=aspnetcore-11.0)\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nReport results using the format described in the [validation testing manual](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68479). This makes it risky as an enterprise boundary.\\n\\nResult: teams either accept the risk of experimental CE or keep building bespoke wrappers on top of the JS API, leading to fragmentation and duplicated effort.\\n\\n### Describe the solution you\\u0026#39;d like\\n\\n**Request A (preferred):** A clear roadmap to **graduate Blazor Custom Elements** from experimental to supported, with:\\n\\nSupport for **child content / templated components** (slot/RenderFragment mapping).\\n\\nDocumented **parameter update** semantics (properties vs attributes; rich object props update without re-add).\\n\\nA standard **eventing model** (DOM CustomEvent with typed detail, bubbles+composed across Shadow DOM).\\n\\nExplicit **lifecycle guarantees** (when instances are mounted/unmounted; disposal and cleanup).\\n\\nGuidance for **RCL** assets (/_content/...) and script choice (blazor.webassembly.js / blazor.server.js vs blazor.web.js) for SPA embedding.\\n\\n**Request B (if CE won’t be prioritized):** Explicitly endorse the JS Render API as the long-term contract and ship small official helpers to reduce glue:\\n\\n**1. SPA Bridge SDK (JS/TS):**\\n```\\nawait waitForBlazor();\\nconst inst = await mount(el, \\u0026#34;componentId\\u0026#34;, params); // Date→ISO handled\\nawait update(inst || el, params);                    // live UpdateParams when available; else safe re-add\\ndispose(inst);\\non(el, \\u0026#34;my:event\\u0026#34;, (payload) =\\u0026gt; { ... });            // DOM CustomEvent conventions\\n```\\n\\n- Normalizes Dates/numbers; attaches hostId; enforces bubbles+composed events; guards against concurrent mounts.\\n\\n**2.  Types \\u0026amp; codegen:**\\n\\nTypeScript typings for component parameters and event payloads (source from component metadata) to give strong types in host apps.\\n\\n**3. Optional wrappers:**\\n\\nThin custom-element facade generator that uses the JS API under the hood (declarative  for consumers, stable internals).\\n\\nTiny framework shims: Vue component, React wrapper, Angular directive — all built on the same bridge SDK.\\n\\n**4. Docs \\u0026amp; guidance:**\\n\\nUpdate docs to present one endorsed path (JS API + helpers) with examples for micro-frontends and design systems, and clarify blazor.web.js readiness criteria.\\n\\n\\n**Acceptance criteria (either path):**\\n\\n- A supported way to embed Razor components cross-framework with stable lifecycle, typed params, and rich events—without each team writing bespoke glue.\\n- Clear statement on long-term support (CE vs JS API) and capabilities scope.\\n\\n### Additional context\\n\\n**- Why now**: Many orgs are standardizing on Web Components for cross-framework reuse. Razor components can participate—if Blazor provides a supported CE story or endorses the JS API with helpers.\\n\\n**- Minimal repro / helper prototype (attached, see lower):**\\nA runnable sample demonstrating both patterns:\\n\\n- JS Render API: mount a Razor component with a rich params object (date/bool/number/nested) and receive a rich payload back via CustomEvent.\\n- Custom Element facade: a thin  wrapper that calls rootComponents.add(...) internally, exposing a clean declarative tag while retaining explicit dispose() control.\\n\\n**Impact if unaddressed**: Teams continue to ship ad-hoc wrappers; inconsistent contracts; pressure to adopt experimental CE; slower adoption of Razor components in heterogeneous SPA estates.\\n\\n**- What feedback would help you most:**\\n  - Whether CE is intended to graduate (and rough timeframe).\\n  - If not, confirmation that the JS Render API + official helpers is the long-term direction, so we can align internal standards and avoid bespoke solutions.\\n\\nPlease see:  https://github.com/paulvanbladel/BlazorWebComponentsInteropDemo\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/64216\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"paulvanbladel\",\"id\":4886272,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/paulvanbladel\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/4886272?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-10-31T10:14:13Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-10-31T10:27:54Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The .NET/JS interop can continue using shared memory if we find it\\u0026#39;s necessary to have good perf on those older browsers (and thread safety is not difficult because it\\u0026#39;s all synchronous).\\n * **In a web worker (background thread) on more up-to-date browsers**. The .NET/JS interop will need to work by serializing any data that is being transferred rather than passing pointers [1].\\n\\nThis will be advantageous because then, even if your .NET code does something that locks up the CPU (such as a GC cycle), the UI will remain perfectly smooth (e.g., during animations or scrolling, or while the user is typing quickly into a textbox).\\n\\nThe existing UI update mechanism is designed around transferring batches of minimal diffs from .NET to JS, so it shouldn\\u0026#39;t be hugely difficult to have it express those diffs as serialized data rather than pointers into the WASM memory space. We\\u0026#39;ll have to be careful around things like event handling to ensure that the asynchrony can\\u0026#39;t result in inconsistency of behaviour versus the synchronous single-threaded model. For example, we will need to force all event delivery to be async as far as the JS side is concerned, even in the non-worker-thread case.\\n\\n*[1] Strictly speaking, we could also do it with shared memory on even newer browsers that support SharedArrayBuffer. But if we can get satisfactory perf without this, it would be better to serialize because it would mean fewer combinations of browser scenarios, and saves us having to deal with potentially complex thread-safety concerns on the .NET side.*\",\"state\":\"open\",\"state_reason\":\"reopened\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/5475\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"severity-minor\",\"affected-very-few\",\"not-on-roadmap\"],\"assignees\":[\"pavelsavara\"],\"milestone\":\".NET 12 Planning\",\"comments\":14,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":22,\"+1\":21,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":1,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2018-02-19T17:05:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T12:05:29Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":67768,\"title\":\"Run Blazor WebAssembly in a Web Worker\",\"state\":\"CLOSED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67768\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Its environment, its culture and any settings it reads all had to be baked in or fetched after it had already started. This validates that the server can decide these before the app starts in the browser, so each visitor\\u0026#39;s app comes up already set up for them.\\n\\n## Minimum build\\n\\n.NET 11 Preview 7 or later.\\n\\n## Configurations to cover\\n\\n* Blazor Web App\\n  * [ ] Static SSR\\n  * [ ] Interactive Server\\n  * [x] Interactive WebAssembly\\n  * [x] Interactive Auto\\n* [ ] Standalone WebAssembly\\n* [ ] Hybrid (MAUI)\\n\\n## Also exercise\\n\\n* [ ] Published output\\n* [ ] An existing .NET 10 app upgraded to .NET 11\\n* [ ] Trimming or ahead-of-time compilation\\n* [ ] More than one server instance, or a proxy in front\\n* [ ] Hot Reload\\n* [ ] An IDE as well as the command line\\n* [ ] Container\\n\\n## Setup\\n\\nThe app needs resources for at least two languages so that a culture change is visible, and something in the UI that behaves differently between environments.\\n\\nThe properties this scenario exercises live under `BrowserOptions.InteractiveWebAssembly`:\\n\\n* `ApplicationCulture`\\n* `EnvironmentName`\\n* `EnvironmentVariables`, a dictionary the server fills in\\n\\nThey are set through `MapRazorComponents().WithBrowserOptions(...)` in server startup, or per request through a `` component in the page.\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nA Blazor Web App whose WebAssembly side has its culture, environment and a couple of environment variables decided by the server. Show all of these on a page: the environment the app believes it is in, the culture it formats dates and numbers with, some translated text, and the values it read from its environment variables.\\n\\nMake the choices depend on the request, for example taking `ApplicationCulture` from the signed-in user\\u0026#39;s profile or a preference cookie, and `EnvironmentName` from a query string, so that different visitors get different answers. Include a page whose content is environment-dependent so the effect is visible in the UI rather than only in a debug readout.\\n\\n## Things to try\\n\\n* Loading the app with each culture and checking dates, numbers and translated text.\\n* Loading with each environment and checking the environment-dependent content.\\n* Changing the preference that drives the culture, then reloading.\\n* Opening two browsers at once with different preferences.\\n* Comparing the first render of the page with what appears once the app is running in the browser.\\n* Giving `ApplicationCulture` a culture the app has no translations for.\\n* Giving `EnvironmentName` a value of your own invention rather than a standard one.\\n* Setting several `EnvironmentVariables`, including one with an empty value.\\n* In Interactive Auto, the first visit and a later visit once the app has been cached.\\n* Navigating to a WebAssembly page rather than loading it directly, so startup happens after an enhanced navigation.\\n\\n## Expected behavior\\n\\nThe WebAssembly side comes up already set up for this visitor, without a visible correction afterwards.\\n\\n### Must hold\\n\\n* The WebAssembly side reports the culture, environment and environment variables the server chose from its first render, without visibly correcting itself afterwards.\\n* Dates and numbers format according to `ApplicationCulture`, and translated text appears in it.\\n* Two browsers with different preferences receive different results at the same time.\\n* A culture with no translations falls back as it would otherwise, and an `EnvironmentName` of your own invention is accepted as given.\\n* A WebAssembly page reached by navigation gets the same values as one loaded directly.\\n\\n### Expected differences between configurations\\n\\n* In Interactive Auto the first visit runs on the server and later visits run in the browser, so note whether the culture, environment and variables match across both.\\n\\n## Documentation to use\\n\\n* [ASP.NET Core Blazor globalization and localization](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/blazor/globalization-localization?view=aspnetcore-11.0)\\n* [ASP.NET Core Blazor environments](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/blazor/fundamentals/environments?view=aspnetcore-11.0)\\n* [ASP.NET Core Blazor configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/blazor/fundamentals/configuration?view=aspnetcore-11.0)\\n\\nThe API names above were taken from the shipped code, not from docs. If you cannot find this documented anywhere, say so in the report.\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nReport results using the format described in the [validation testing manual](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68479). Include link to a repository with the test app.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68816\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"oroztocil\",\"id\":79744616,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/oroztocil\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/79744616?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Validation\",\"validation-scenario\"],\"milestone\":\"11.0-rc2\",\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-26T15:24:19Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T15:25:02Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For example:\\n\\n * Render batches are communicated to JS via zero-copy shared memory rather than by serialization\\n * Events triggered from JS are always processed synchronously by .NET, so there\\u0026#39;s no need to queue them\\n\\nAt first glance, it appears to work with `true`, but that\\u0026#39;s a mirage: it does *not* guarantee correctness in that mode, because the core single-threadedness assumption is violated. For example, JS might raise event 2 before event 1 finished processing, and by the time event 1 is done, there might not even be an event 2 handler any more and then you have an error.\\n\\n### Why we\\u0026#39;re only just encountering this now\\n\\n1. We didn\\u0026#39;t have multithreading before\\n2. Even to the extent that we did have an early preview of multithreading, it worked by running .NET on the browser UI thread, so we could define that as the sync context and then all the same assumptions would remain valid within that sync context. But now .NET WebAssembly has just moved to the new \\u0026#34;deputy thread\\u0026#34; multithreading model (i.e., all .NET code is on a background worker), these assumptions are no longer valid (e.g., because the UI thread\\u0026#39;s JS can no longer communicate with .NET in a synchronous, blocking manner).\\n\\n### Ensuring correctness\\n\\nWe\\u0026#39;ve already solved all these problems in our other hosting environments, Server and WebView, because they\\u0026#39;ve always been innately asynchronous from the beginning. We would need to generalize/port all these mechanisms so they are shared with or copied by the WebAssembly renderer, JS interop, eventing system, etc.:\\n\\n- [ ] Change rendering to serialize renderbatches to JS instead of doing shared-memory reads\\n- [ ] Change the rendering flow so that the renderer\\u0026#39;s `UpdateDisplayAsync` returns a `Task` that doesn\\u0026#39;t complete until the JS side sends back an explicit acknowledgement of that renderbatch\\n- [ ] Review JS interop to make sure any low-level assumptions we\\u0026#39;ve made about synchrony during the internals of message passing are replaced by async assumptions\\n- [ ] Do the above without changing things for the **single-threaded** WebAssembly flavour, since (1) it would be breaking if for example synchronous UI updates became async, and (2) those perf optimizations are there for a reason, and we don\\u0026#39;t want to make rendering many times more expensive in cases where you\\u0026#39;d be serializing huge strings, for example. It\\u0026#39;s OK to have significant behavioral and performance changes when people opt into multithreading, but not when they don\\u0026#39;t.\\n\\n### Approach\\n\\nAs a broad strategy, I think we can:\\n\\n * Factor out some new `WebRenderer` subclass called something like `AsyncWebRenderer` that holds the common logic around serializing renderbatches and accepting the async renderbatch acknowledgements from JS. This can then be used by all of Server, WebView, and multithreaded-WebAssembly.\\n * Use our WebView implementation as the reference for how a complete, async-safe rendering and eventing model should work, because this was more recently implemented than Server and is generally simpler and cleaner. There\\u0026#39;s not a huge amount of code in it, really. If some extra work is needed to queue event notifications, for example, we should see that clearly from the WebView code.\\n\\nI suspect it\\u0026#39;s not necessary to have two different builds of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly`. The total amount of code that should differ between the threaded and not-threaded won\\u0026#39;t be very much. I expect we can just have two different `Renderer` subclasses and some if/else branches in the JS code.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54365\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"triaged\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-threading\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":26,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":47,\"+1\":30,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":17,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-03-05T10:02:51Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-04-21T00:06:24Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":true,\"has_children\":false,\"parent\":{\"number\":17730,\"title\":\"Real multithreading in Blazor WebAssembly\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17730\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

This proposal is that support.\\n\\nBlazor discovers a great deal about an application at runtime. Which components exist and how to construct them; which of their members are parameters, and how to read and write each one; which members carry `[Inject]` and what service each wants; which members of a model are reachable through `@bind`; which methods are `[JSInvokable]` and how to dispatch to them; and how to serialize the values flowing through all of the above. Today every one of those questions is answered by walking `MemberInfo` and invoking reflectively, and the JSON carrying the values is serialized through the reflection-based contract resolver.\\n\\nAll of that information is knowable at compile time. The Razor compiler already sees the component graph; the attributes are already there in source. What is missing is a way for a source generator to write that knowledge down, and a way for the framework to use it when it is available.\\n\\nThat is what this API is: **a contract between generated code and the framework, describing what the framework currently discovers by reflection.** When an application supplies it, Blazor reads parameters, resolves injectables, walks bind models, dispatches JS interop and serializes state through ordinary generated code. When it is absent, nothing changes and the existing reflection paths run exactly as before.\\n\\nThe Dashboard is what has driven the shape here — it is a real application that exercises all of these paths at once, which is why we used it to validate the design rather than a synthetic sample. But nothing in this API is specific to it: any Blazor Server application can supply the same metadata, and applications that stay JIT-compiled benefit too, through less runtime discovery, less metadata kept alive for trimming, and serialization that no longer depends on reflection being enabled.\\n\\nBecause generated code lives in the **application\\u0026#39;s own assembly**, every type and member it touches has to be public. That is why this proposal is as large as it is. Nothing here is meant to be written by hand: an application author adds a single call, `AddComponentMetadata()`, and the generator produces the rest. The types sit in `*.Infrastructure` namespaces, and everything proposed here carries `[Experimental(\\u0026#34;ASPNETCORE9004\\u0026#34;)]` so the shape can still move while we take more applications through it.\\n\\n## Proposed API\\n\\n### `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components` — what the generator writes down\\n\\n```diff\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Infrastructure;\\n\\n+[Experimental(\\u0026#34;ASPNETCORE9004\\u0026#34;, UrlFormat = \\u0026#34;https://aka.ms/aspnet/analyzer/{0}\\u0026#34;)]\\n+public sealed class ComponentDescriptor\\n+{\\n+    public Type Type { get; init; }\\n+    public Func? In Blazor we use the .NET trimmer to significantly reduce the publish size of Blazor WebAssembly apps. However, we don\\u0026#39;t currently use the .NET trimmer to its fullest potential. We currently configure the trimmer in a partial mode, which only trims assemblies that are explicitly marked as trimmable. This typically means that the app assembly itself and many dependencies are not trimmed. This is a conservative setting that optimizes for maintaining functionality over reducing app size. \\n\\nThe default trim mode for the .NET trimmer is to trim everything. This is the mode used by the .NET Native AOT workloads.Analyzers provide warnings if there are code paths in the app that are not safe to trim. Given how sensitive web apps are to download size and load time, it seems like doing full trimming should be the goal for Blazor.\\n\\nEnabling support for full trimming also is a potential solution to enabling a [single project model for Blazor Web Apps](#49079) that target both server and browser. When you multitarget a project, everything in the project is built for both targets unless you indicated otherwise. This is problematic for browser scenarios because you may potentially bring in dependencies, components, and code into the browser targeted build that are only needed on the server. However, if we could enable full trimming *and* indicate to the trimmer which components are setup to render on WebAssembly, then the browser build could be aggressively trimmed to remove any unwanted code and dependencies.\\n\\nEnabling support for full .NET trimming typically means removing any dynamic code path that are based on reflection. We would need to make Blazor apps trimmer friendly by removing this code using techniques like source generators. For example, in Blazor we use reflection as part of the component discovery process and in the render tree builder code generated by the Razor compiler. We\\u0026#39;re already working on enabling [component discovery through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48767). We also have on our backlog to [handle component parameters through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/29550). There may be other related work items as well.\\n\\nThere is also ecosystem impact of enabling full trimming by default. Many .NET libraries are not setup for trimming and would potentially need to be updated. It will take some time to work through these issues with the Blazor community. provides first-class support for all Blazor hosting models (WebAssembly, Server, and Blazor Web) within .NET Aspire applications, using a Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern via a **Blazor Gateway** component.\\n\\n### Key Features\\n\\n**Blazor Gateway** provides:\\n- Optimized serving of WebAssembly static assets with `MapStaticAssets` (compression \\u0026amp; caching)\\n- API proxying to backend services (eliminates CORS requirements)\\n- Configuration flow to WebAssembly clients via `/_blazor/_configuration`\\n- Session affinity for multi-replica Blazor Server scenarios\\n- Replacement for the Dev Server in both development and production\\n\\n### Hosting Scenarios\\n\\n| Scenario | Gateway Configuration |\\n|----------|----------------------|\\n| Standalone WebAssembly + Aspire | Separate node (defined in AppHost) |\\n| Hosted WebAssembly | Embedded in host project |\\n| Blazor Server (single replica) | Not required |\\n| Blazor Server (multi-replica) | Separate node (load balancing + session affinity) |\\n| Blazor Web (Server + WASM) | Embedded or separate (based on replica count) |\\n\\n### Related Work Items\\n\\n- [ ] Server-side configuration endpoint for Blazor Web (#30116)\\n- [ ] IHostedService support in WebAssembly (#63637)\\n- [ ] Environment variables in IConfiguration by default (#64576)\\n- [ ] Gateway package for standalone Blazor WebAssembly (#64573)\\n- [ ] WebAssembly service defaults template (#64574)\\n- [ ] Consider enabling MetricsSupport/EventSourceSupport by default (#64575)\\n- [ ] Register Components metric and tracing by default on webassembly host The \\u0026#34;weather forecast\\u0026#34; page simply generates data on the client and thus only demonstrates how to render a table, not how to fetch data.\\n\\nActually calling a server API in all generality, accounting for all the main ways of setting up a site, is complicated by several factors, as pointed out by @mrpmorris:\\n\\n * Deal with prerendering or auto mode. In these cases, you have to be able to load the data when running on WebAssembly *and* when running on the server. So you must either:\\n   * Register `HttpClient` in DI with a base address on both server and client, and have the server call itself via HTTP\\n   * Or, have some interface representing the datastore, and set up both server and client implementations\\n * Avoid the double-render problem whereby the data is loaded twice (once for prerendering, once for interactivity)\\n   * This is more complicated with per-page interactivity, since enanced nav doesn\\u0026#39;t currently work with persistent state\\n * Make this work sensibly with auth, including for both client and server data access\\n\\nWhile typical apps don\\u0026#39;t usually have to solve all these problems simultaneously, we need to be able to demonstrate convenient, flexible patterns that do compose well with all the features and are clean enough to put them in the project template.\\n\\nSolving this nicely likely depends on implementing some other features like https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/51584\\n\\n# Note for community: Recommendation for .NET 8 developers\\n\\nAs mentioned above, typical apps don\\u0026#39;t normally have to solve all these problems. It\\u0026#39;s always been simple to load data from the server with Blazor WebAssembly and that is still the case in .NET 8.\\n\\nThe easiest path is simply to disable WebAssembly prerendering, because then just about all the complexity vanishes. Whenever you used rendermode `WebAssembly` (e.g., in `App.razor`), replace it with `new WebAssemblyRenderMode(prerender: false)`.\\n\\nAt that point your UI is just running in the browser and you can make `HttpClient` calls to the server as normal.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/55307\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-templates\"],\"assignees\":[\"danroth27\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":23,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":27,\"+1\":25,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":2},\"created_at\":\"2024-04-23T08:51:59Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T18:04:42Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Please describe the problem.\\n\\n\\n[WebMCP](https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp) is an emerging web platform API that allows web pages to expose **in‑page “tools”** (with natural‑language descriptions and structured schemas) to AI agents and assistive technologies via a browser surface (`navigator.modelContext`). The tools are registered and executed **in the client page context**, enabling human‑in‑the‑loop, cooperative workflows where users and agents share UI state.\\n\\nToday, ASP.NET Core developers who want to experiment with or adopt WebMCP patterns must piece together:\\n- ad‑hoc JavaScript for tool registration and lifecycle management,\\n- custom schema generation for tool inputs/outputs,\\n- inconsistent security, confirmation, and authorization patterns,\\n- and framework‑specific glue for Razor Pages/MVC vs. Blazor (especially Blazor WASM and interactive components).\\n\\nThis results in:\\n- **Duplicated, fragile implementations** across apps and teams  \\n- **Unclear guidance** on safe and idiomatic usage within ASP.NET Core  \\n- A missed opportunity to align WebMCP with **Blazor’s strengths** as a client‑side, stateful UI framework\\n\\nASP.NET Core does not need to implement the WebMCP browser API itself, but it currently lacks **first‑class guidance and primitives** to make WebMCP adoption straightforward, consistent, and secure across its supported frontend models.\\n\\n\\u0026gt; **NOTE:** Filed as a result of a question at MVP Summit in the C# MCP SDK presentation.\\n\\n### Describe the solution you\\u0026#39;d like\\n\\n\\nAt a high level, introduce **first‑class guidance (and optionally lightweight libraries)** that make ASP.NET Core a strong platform for *authoring* WebMCP‑enabled applications.\\n\\nSpecifically:\\n\\n### A. Official guidance\\nProvide documentation that explains:\\n- What WebMCP is (and is not), and how it differs from backend MCP / API integrations\\n- How WebMCP concepts (tools, schemas, lifecycle) map onto ASP.NET Core patterns\\n- When to prefer Razor Pages/MVC vs. Blazor (especially WASM and interactive components)\\n\\n### B. Blazor‑first authoring patterns\\nBecause WebMCP tools run in the page’s client context, Blazor is a particularly strong fit. Consider:\\n- An idiomatic way to register WebMCP tools from Blazor components or services\\n- Mapping tool handlers to .NET methods via JS interop\\n- Clear lifecycle semantics (register/unregister on render/dispose)\\n- Hosting‑model considerations (WASM vs. Server vs. hybrid Web Apps)\\n\\n### C. Razor Pages / MVC declarative story\\nFor server‑rendered apps:\\n- Explore Tag Helpers or conventions that align HTML forms/actions with WebMCP’s declarative approach\\n- Provide guidance on schema generation, validation, and anti‑forgery considerations\\n\\n### D. Secure‑by‑default recommendations\\nAt a minimum, documentation (and possibly helpers) for:\\n- Differentiating read‑only vs. mutating tools\\n- User confirmation patterns for agent‑initiated actions\\n- Avoiding unintended tool exposure (iframes, embedded contexts, etc.)\\n- Logging and observability for tool invocation\\n\\n### E. Samples over deep framework changes\\nThis could initially ship as:\\n- Documentation plus samples\\n- An experimental or opt‑in package\\n- A small set of framework‑owned helpers\\n\\nrather than committing to deep framework integration before the WebMCP specification stabilizes.\\n\\n**Alternative considered:** Waiting until WebMCP is further along the standards track. The downside is fragmented experimentation and lost opportunity for early feedback from ASP.NET Core developers during the spec’s formative phase.\\n\\n\\n### Additional context\\n\\n\\n- WebMCP is currently a **W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group draft**, and the API surface is still evolving.\\n- This proposal is intentionally scoped to **authoring support**, not implementing or polyfilling the browser API.\\n- This aligns with ASP.NET Core’s historical approach to emerging web platform features: provide clear guidance, good defaults, and opt‑in helpers without forcing adoption.\\n- Early alignment would allow ASP.NET Core (especially Blazor) apps to participate in and help shape emerging “agentic web” patterns while keeping humans firmly in control.\\n- [WebMCP is available for early preview (Chrome)](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/webmcp-epp) \",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/65981\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"jongalloway\",\"id\":68539,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/jongalloway\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/68539?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":4,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-03-25T22:25:19Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-03-30T01:14:52Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Adds a comment to an existing GitHub issue, pull request, or discussion. Use this to provide feedback, answer questions, or add information to an existing conversation. For creating new items, use create_issue, create_discussion, or create_pull_request instead. IMPORTANT: Comments are subject to validation constraints enforced by the MCP server - maximum 65536 characters for the complete comment (including footer which is added automatically), 10 mentions (@username), and 50 links. Exceeding these limits will result in an immediate error with specific guidance. NOTE: Discussion comments are disabled for this workflow because discussions:write permission is not available. Set 'discussions: true' in the workflow's safe-outputs.add-comment configuration to enable discussion comments and request this permission. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 comment(s) can be added. Target: *. This tool records a real comment intent. Do not use it for placeholder comments, auth checks, or probing. Call it only when the final comment body is ready; otherwise use noop or report_incomplete.

For creating new issues with labels, use create_issue with the labels property instead. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 3 label(s) can be added. INTENT ENCOURAGED: Include rationale (string, max 280 chars) and confidence (exactly one of: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) with each call. safeoutputs.description: Report that a tool or capability needed to complete the task is not available, or share any information you deem important about missing functionality or limitations. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because the required functionality is missing or access is restricted. safeoutputs.description: Log a transparency message when no significant actions are needed. This is distinct from noop (no action needed) — it indicates an active failure that prevented the task from running.
